disposition_reason: FDA CFSAN retail survey of 144 US-purchased cocoa powders (incl. drink mixes), dark chocolates, milk chocolates and cocoa nibs analysed for Cd and Pb by ICP-MS; prints form-level summary tables, subgroup means in figure captions and a full per-sample appendix of all 144 Cd and 144 Pb results.
disposition_locator: Abstract; Methods (Samples); Tables 3-5; Figure 1, 2, 5, 6 captions; appendix pp. 19-27

study.material_scope: retail cocoa powder (including cocoa drink mixes), dark chocolate, milk chocolate, cocoa nibs; chocolate with inclusions excluded
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market: retail in Prince George's County, Maryland, USA and online. Growing origin (Latin America vs Africa) taken from product labels and company websites, not verified; 23 dark, 22 milk and 20 powder samples had no or multi-country origin.
study.sampling_unit: retail products (standard consumer packages; 4 were 10-lb commercial chocolate blocks), 67 manufacturers; one ~20 g homogenised portion per product
study.method: FDA Elemental Analysis Manual 4.7: microwave digestion (UltraClave, HNO3/H2O2, 250 C) and ICP-MS (Agilent 8800, He collision mode); Pb as sum of 206/207/208, Cd 111
study.lod_loq: Cd LOD 0.408 ug/kg, LOQ 3.71 ug/kg; Pb LOD 1.20 ug/kg, LOQ 10.9 ug/kg (Table 2). Values between LOD and LOQ reported as trace values and included.
study.qa: Table 2 (n=7): Cd NIST SRM 2384 baking chocolate 81.8±2.3 vs certified 73.4±7.7 ug/kg (112%, z +1.1); Cd FDA in-house cocoa powder 364±9.4 vs 368±13 (99%, z -0.3); Pb SRM 2384 36.9±5.4 vs 35.7±4.6 (103%, z +0.3); Pb FDA cocoa powder 119±23.1 vs 107±11 (111%, z +1.1). Duplicates and pre/post-digestion spikes at 10% intervals, two method blanks per batch, 80-120% acceptance; appendix prints duplicate RPDs of 0-17%.
study.percent_cocoa_distribution: Table 5 (label %): dark chocolate 50-64% 8, 65-79% 29, 80-94% 13, 95-100% 4 (3 not specified); milk chocolate 20-34% 12, 35-49% 12, 50-64% 9, 65-79% 2 (6 not specified); cocoa powder 20-34% 1, 35-49% 1, 50-64% 2, 95-100% 26 (all 100%) (9 not specified); cocoa nibs 95-100% 7. Verified against the rendered page; totals reconcile with n=57/41/39/7 and 126 labelled products.

Form means: milk chocolate Cd 60 ug/kg vs dark 270 vs cocoa powder 700 vs nibs 620; Pb milk 10, dark 30, powder 110 ug/kg.
controls.locator: Results p. 6; Figures 3-4; Tables 3-5; ANCOVA p. 7

controls.comparator: label-declared Latin America vs Africa origin, adjusting for percent cocoa
controls.outcome: ANCOVA (log-transformed, n=76, interaction not significant, product type not modelled): origin effect on Cd p<0.001 (model R2 0.60); no significant origin effect on Pb p=0.18 (R2 0.14). contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary says purchases were in December 2015; primary says December 2015 and January 2016.
Stored summary names Latin American (Brazil, Ecuador, Peru) and West African (Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana) countries; the primary text does not list any origin countries, only Latin America vs Africa.
Stored summary gives form sample sizes as "(subset of 144)"; the primary prints n = 57 dark, 41 milk, 39 cocoa powder, 7 nibs.
Stored summary omits that the cocoa powder group includes sweetened cocoa drink mixes with sugars and dairy solids (Table 3 footnote a).
Stored summary describes chocolate portioning as "consistent with FDA preparation protocols"; primary says ~20 g portions taken from various areas of each bar, frozen at -30 C and tube-milled.
Stored summary implications recommend certification floors and benchmark pools; these are not in the source.
unresolved: Figures 1-4 (concentration vs percent cocoa, means and SD by % band and product type) and Figures 5-6 (box plots by Latin America vs Africa) print no numeric values beyond those in captions; not digitised. Origin-group means and SDs for this dataset are printed in Abt & Robin 2020 (abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate) Table 1 and are extracted there; they reconcile with this paper (weighted means of Africa, Latin America and unclassified groups reproduce the Table 3/4 form means).
The appendix does not link sample IDs to percent cocoa or origin, so per-band or per-origin statistics cannot be recomputed from sample_values.

Appendix values are rounded to 0.01 mg/kg; Pb results printed as 0.00 or 0.01 cannot be resolved below 10 ug/kg. Interpretation of the appendix "<" flag as trace (LOD-LOQ) is inferred: per-form counts of "<" flags (dark 16, milk 31, powder 3, nibs 4) match Table 4 footnote b exactly, and the three unflagged 0.00 nib Pb results (samples 134-136) match footnote c (<LOD).

Duplicate RPD values in the appendix are not reliably attributable to specific rows where sample IDs wrap across lines (e.g. near samples 105/106, 125/126, 131), so they are not attached to sample_values.

Read from the accepted manuscript (Food Addit Contam B, DOI 10.1080/19393210.2017.1420700, posted 8 Jan 2018), not the typeset version (2018, 11, 92-102); page locators use the manuscript page numbers.

Recomputed from the appendix: form means/medians/SDs/min/max reproduce Tables 3 and 4 to printed precision (e.g. Cd powder mean 0.702, SD 0.833; Pb nib mean 0.003 with three zeros), so no integrity conflict found beyond the authors' zero imputation for nib Pb.
notes: Authors conclude levels do not present a safety concern relative to JECFA 2013 Cd assessment and FDA Pb-in-candy guidance (author judgement, cited for context only). JECFA (2013) cited: high consumers of cocoa products 30-69% of PTMI (25 ug/kg bw per month) for adults and 96% for children 0.5-12 years.
